headline: Internal Party Database Allegedly Experiences 'Self-Correcting Ghost' That Automatically Deletes Names Of People Holding Coffee
body:
Q: Mr. Sharma, as the Chief Digital Archivist for the party, can you explain why several high-profile members are suddenly disappearing from the digital draft of the upcoming assembly list?

A: It’s not a vendetta, it’s a firmware update. Our new AI-driven database, 'Swayam-Shuddhi,' has an experimental feature designed to filter out 'energy-draining entities.' It turns out the algorithm identified a direct correlation between holding a cup of lukewarm cappuccino and lower party morale, so it simply purged those profiles.

Q: But these are veteran leaders, not just random files. Are you saying the software decided they were 'un-draftable' simply because of their drink choice?

A: Precisely. The code doesn't see seniority; it sees beverage choices. If a leader appears in a photo holding a latte, the system assumes they are preparing for a career in travel blogging and removes their name to save bandwidth. It’s actually quite efficient; we’ve saved 400MB of storage space this week alone.

Q: So, how do these members get back on the list? Do they have to renounce their caffeine addiction?

A: They can apply for a 'Reinstatement of Relevance' ticket. They just need to upload a photo of themselves drinking cutting chai while looking intensely at a thick, dust-covered binder. The software responds much better to the aesthetic of a person drowning in paperwork than one enjoying a mid-afternoon break.
caption: Software updates are getting personal! Local party IT team claims the new 'Anti-Coffee' filter is just a feature, not a bug. Is your name safe from the purge? #PartyPolitics #TechFail #DigitalVendetta (satire)
